safety_boundary: No financial advice, live trading, credentials, private exchange actions, or production-readiness claims.
obsolescence_triggers: material changes to Basel or IOSCO standards
major crypto or FX venue-structure changes
new evidence on backtest multiple-testing controls
changes to project data, execution, cost, or validation models

evidence.claim: FX research must account for dealer, customer, venue and instrument segmentation rather than treating the market as one homogeneous order book.
evidence.title: Triennial Central Bank Survey of foreign exchange and OTC derivatives markets in 2022
evidence.applicability: FX spot, forwards, swaps and options; useful for defining venue and counterparty dimensions in research metadata.
evidence.limitations: Aggregate survey evidence does not provide strategy-level execution costs or intraday order-book dynamics.

evidence.claim: Prices, spreads and liquidity reflect information asymmetry, inventory and trading mechanisms; backtests should model execution assumptions explicitly.
evidence.title: Market Microstructure Theory
evidence.applicability: Conceptual foundation for spread, liquidity, price formation and execution modeling across FX and crypto venues.
evidence.limitations: Predates modern crypto venues, perpetual funding and current high-frequency market design.
obsolescence_triggers: new synthesis superseding core microstructure assumptions

evidence.claim: Crypto market-integrity recommendations identify fragmentation, conflicts and venue risks, but they do not establish that crypto and FX microstructure are interchangeable.
evidence.title: Policy Recommendations for Crypto and Digital Asset Markets
evidence.applicability: Crypto venue governance, conflicts, custody, market abuse and cross-border fragmentation.
evidence.limitations: Policy recommendations are not empirical estimates of slippage, liquidity or strategy profitability; implementation varies by jurisdiction.

evidence.claim: Risk assessment should include tail, liquidity, stress and model limitations rather than relying on a single average-return metric.
evidence.title: Basel Framework: Calculation of RWA for market risk
evidence.applicability: Provides authoritative terminology and stress/model-risk concepts for research controls.
evidence.limitations: Designed for prudential regulation of internationally active banks, not direct sizing rules for a trading strategy.

evidence.claim: A risk measure should be evaluated against explicit axioms and assumptions; no single measure is universally sufficient for nonlinear or liquidity-sensitive exposures.
evidence.title: Coherent Measures of Risk
evidence.publisher_or_authors: Artzner, Philippe; Delbaen, Freddy; Eber, Jean-Marc; Heath, David
evidence.applicability: Foundation for evaluating portfolio risk metrics and aggregation properties.
evidence.limitations: Axiomatic coherence alone does not model execution liquidity, funding, liquidation or regime shifts.
obsolescence_triggers: material change in selected project risk-measure framework

evidence.claim: Regulatory capital standards are useful evidence for control design but should not be presented as proof that a research strategy is safe, sufficiently capitalized or production-ready.
evidence.title: Minimum capital requirements for market risk
evidence.applicability: Boundary-setting for stress testing, model approval and risk governance concepts.
evidence.limitations: Institutional scope, horizons, capital objectives and supervisory overlays differ materially from crypto/FX strategy research.
obsolescence_triggers: replacement by revised consolidated Basel text

evidence.claim: Backtesting compares realized outcomes with model-generated risk measures and requires exception analysis rather than treating a passing statistic as complete validation.
evidence.title: Supervisory framework for the use of backtesting in conjunction with the internal models approach to market risk capital requirements
evidence.applicability: Authoritative precedent for exception counting, model review and fail-closed interpretation of backtest results.
evidence.limitations: Superseded regulatory document focused on market-risk capital models, not alpha-strategy selection.
obsolescence_triggers: project adopts a newer authoritative backtesting standard

evidence.claim: Testing many strategy configurations can create severe backtest overfitting; simple holdout validation may be unreliable after repeated model selection.
evidence.title: The Probability of Backtest Overfitting
evidence.publisher_or_authors: Bailey, David H.; Borwein, Jonathan M.; López de Prado, Marcos; Zhu, Qiji Jim
evidence.applicability: Strategy selection, parameter searches, multiple testing and expected out-of-sample degradation.
evidence.limitations: PBO/CSCV assumptions and implementation choices require adequate sample structure and do not replace cost or market-impact modeling.
obsolescence_triggers: material change in project search procedure

evidence.claim: A positive historical result is not sufficient when data snooping, multiple comparisons, nonstationarity and transaction costs are unresolved.
evidence.title: A Reality Check for Data Snooping
evidence.applicability: Formal warning and testing framework for performance selected from many candidate models.
evidence.limitations: Statistical correction does not establish economic implementability, stable market impact or future regime persistence.
